entry.title: Pure Post Quantum Cryptography TLS with ASP.NET Core
entry.summary: Over the last few years, I have dedicated a lot of space on this blog to the topic of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC). Today, we will peek into the TLS 1.3 handshake. While hybrid mode TLS is the pragmatic choice for today’s internet, understanding how to construct a fully quantum-safe connection is critical for preparing for the deprecation of classical algorithms. In this post, we are going to explore a “pure” PQC TLS stack: Post-Quantum Key Exchange, with Post-Quantum Authentication. We will configure an ASP.NET Core application running on Linux to use ML-DSA-65 for authentication and ML-KEM-768 for key exchange.

entry.title: Creating standard and "observable" instruments: System.Diagnostics.Metrics APIs - Part 3
entry.summary: In this post I discuss the various Instrument types exposed by the System.Diagnostics.Metrics API and show examples from the .NET libraries and ASP.NET Core

entry.title: AI Features in SQL Server 2025
entry.summary: SQL Server 2025 brings practical AI building blocks directly into the database engine: the VECTOR data type, vector indexing, ANN-powered similarity search, and T-SQL functions for embeddings and chunking.

entry.title: From SSMS to Azure OpenAI: How Copilot Actually Works
entry.summary: Copilot inside SSMS is a client feature, not a hosted brain. To function, it must connect to an Azure OpenAI resource in your Azure subscription, using two mandatory pieces of configuration: the resource endpoint and a model deployment name.
